CHAPTER 12 — यक्ष-युधिष्ठिर संवादः (YAKSHA-YUDHISHTHIRA SAMVADAH)

Introduction — कथा-प्रसंगः (The setting)

The यक्षप्रश्न ('the Yaksha's questions') is one of the best-loved episodes of the महाभारत, told in the वनपर्व (Vana Parva, also called Aranya Parva). During their long forest exile (वनवास), the five पाण्डव brothers — युधिष्ठिर, भीम, अर्जुन, नकुल and सहदेव — lived simply in the woods. One day a ब्राह्मण came in distress: a deer had run off carrying away his अरणि (the two wooden sticks used to kindle the sacred fire). Without them the brahmin could not perform his daily fire-rites. The Pandavas at once set out to chase the deer and recover the sticks, but the animal vanished, and the brothers, weary and thirsty (श्रान्ताः तृषिताः), lost their way deep in the forest.

This lesson retells that episode in simple, correct Sanskrit prose, with शब्दार्थ (word meanings), an English translation and the moral (सारः). It then presents famous public-domain प्रश्न-उत्तर verses (the Yaksha's riddles and Yudhishthira's replies) with word meanings, and finally draws a little grammar (व्याकरणम् — सन्धि, विभक्ति, शब्दरूप, धातुरूप) from the text. The theme throughout is wisdom (प्रज्ञा), dharma (धर्मः) and self-control (संयमः): true greatness, the story teaches, lies not in bodily strength but in a calm, wise and righteous mind.

The story in simple Sanskrit (कथा — सरलसंस्कृते)

1) पाण्डवाः वने न्यवसन्। एकदा एकः ब्राह्मणः आगत्य अवदत् — 'मम अरणयः मृगेण अपहृताः।'
   शब्दार्थ: वने = in the forest; न्यवसन् = (they) lived; एकदा = once; ब्राह्मणः = a brahmin; आगत्य = having come; अवदत् = said; अरणयः = fire-churning sticks; मृगेण = by a deer; अपहृताः = were carried off.
   Translation: The Pandavas lived in the forest. Once a brahmin came and said, 'My fire-sticks have been carried off by a deer.'

2) पाण्डवाः मृगम् अन्वधावन्, किन्तु मृगः अन्तर्दधे। ते श्रान्ताः तृषिताः च अभवन्।
   शब्दार्थ: अन्वधावन् = (they) ran after; अन्तर्दधे = disappeared; श्रान्ताः = tired; तृषिताः = thirsty; अभवन् = became.
   Translation: The Pandavas ran after the deer, but it disappeared. They became tired and thirsty.

3) युधिष्ठिरः नकुलम् अवदत् — 'भ्रातः, जलम् अन्विष्य आनय।' नकुलः गत्वा एकं सुन्दरं सरः अपश्यत्।
   शब्दार्थ: भ्रातः = O brother; जलम् = water; अन्विष्य = having searched; आनय = bring; गत्वा = having gone; सरः = a lake; अपश्यत् = saw.
   Translation: Yudhishthira said to Nakula, 'Brother, find water and bring it.' Nakula went and saw a beautiful lake.

4) यदा नकुलः जलं पातुम् इच्छति, तदा अदृश्यः यक्षः अवदत् — 'मा पिब! प्रथमं मम प्रश्नान् उत्तरं देहि, ततः जलं पिब।'
   शब्दार्थ: यदा = when; पातुम् = to drink; इच्छति = wishes; तदा = then; अदृश्यः = unseen; यक्षः = a Yaksha (nature-spirit); मा पिब = do not drink; प्रश्नान् = questions; उत्तरं देहि = give the answer; ततः = then.
   Translation: When Nakula wished to drink, an unseen Yaksha said, 'Do not drink! First answer my questions, then drink.'

5) नकुलः तत् वचनम् अवमन्य जलम् अपिबत्, तत्क्षणम् एव मृतः अभवत्। एवमेव सहदेवः, अर्जुनः, भीमः च क्रमेण आगत्य, यक्षस्य वचनम् अनादृत्य, जलं पीत्वा मृताः अभवन्।
   शब्दार्थ: वचनम् = the words; अवमन्य = disregarding; अपिबत् = drank; तत्क्षणम् एव = that very moment; मृतः = dead; एवमेव = in the same way; क्रमेण = one by one; अनादृत्य = ignoring; पीत्वा = having drunk.
   Translation: Nakula disregarded those words, drank the water, and died that very instant. In the same way Sahadeva, Arjuna and Bhima came one by one, ignored the Yaksha's words, drank, and died.
   सारः (Moral): Even the strong and skilful fall when they act carelessly and ignore wise counsel; heedlessness (प्रमादः) leads to ruin.

6) अन्ते युधिष्ठिरः भ्रातॄन् अन्विष्यन् तत्र आगच्छत्। सः चतुरः भ्रातॄन् मृतान् दृष्ट्वा भृशं दुःखितः अभवत्।
   शब्दार्थ: अन्ते = at last; भ्रातॄन् = the brothers; अन्विष्यन् = searching; दृष्ट्वा = having seen; भृशम् = greatly; दुःखितः = grieved.
   Translation: At last Yudhishthira, searching for his brothers, came there. Seeing his four brothers dead, he was deeply grieved.

7) यक्षः पुनः अवदत् — 'अहम् एतत् सरः रक्षामि। मम प्रश्नान् उत्तरं दत्त्वा एव जलं पिब।' युधिष्ठिरः शान्तः अवदत् — 'पृच्छ, यक्ष; यथाबुद्धि उत्तरं दास्यामि।'
   शब्दार्थ: रक्षामि = (I) guard; दत्त्वा = having given; शान्तः = calm; पृच्छ = ask; यथाबुद्धि = according to (my) understanding; दास्यामि = (I) shall give.
   Translation: The Yaksha said again, 'I guard this lake. Only after answering my questions may you drink.' Yudhishthira calmly said, 'Ask, O Yaksha; I shall answer to the best of my understanding.'
   सारः (Moral): The wise person meets even a threat with calmness (संयमः) and humility, and respects righteous rules.

8) यक्षः बहून् धर्मविषयकान् प्रश्नान् अपृच्छत्। युधिष्ठिरः प्रज्ञया सर्वेषां प्रश्नानाम् उचितम् उत्तरम् अददात्। यक्षः तुष्टः अभवत्।
   शब्दार्थ: बहून् = many; धर्मविषयकान् = concerning dharma; प्रज्ञया = with wisdom; सर्वेषाम् = of all; उचितम् = proper; तुष्टः = pleased.
   Translation: The Yaksha asked many questions about dharma. Yudhishthira, with wisdom, gave the proper answer to all of them. The Yaksha was pleased.

9) तुष्टः यक्षः अवदत् — 'तव एकं भ्रातरं जीवयामि; वृणु।' युधिष्ठिरः 'नकुलः जीवतु' इति अवदत्।
   शब्दार्थ: तव = your; जीवयामि = (I) shall bring to life; वृणु = choose; जीवतु = let (him) live; इति = thus.
   Translation: The pleased Yaksha said, 'I shall revive one of your brothers; choose.' Yudhishthira said, 'Let Nakula live.'

10) यक्षः विस्मितः अपृच्छत् — 'भीमः बलवान्, अर्जुनः वीरः; तौ त्यक्त्वा किमर्थं नकुलं वृणोषि?' युधिष्ठिरः अवदत् — 'अहं कुन्त्याः पुत्रः जीवामि; माद्र्याः अपि एकः पुत्रः जीवतु इति मे धर्मः। समता एव धर्मः।'
   शब्दार्थ: विस्मितः = astonished; बलवान् = strong; वीरः = brave; तौ = those two; त्यक्त्वा = leaving aside; किमर्थम् = why; वृणोषि = do you choose; कुन्त्याः = of Kunti; माद्र्याः = of Madri; समता = fairness/equality; एव = indeed.
   Translation: Astonished, the Yaksha asked, 'Bhima is strong, Arjuna is brave; leaving those two, why do you choose Nakula?' Yudhishthira said, 'I, a son of Kunti, am alive; let one son of Madri also live — that is my duty. Fairness itself is dharma.'
   सारः (Moral): Yudhishthira's choice shows आनृशंस्य (non-cruelty, compassion) and impartiality — he places justice above personal advantage.

11) यक्षः अतीव प्रसन्नः सन् सर्वान् चतुरः भ्रातॄन् अजीवयत्। सः यक्षः वस्तुतः धर्मः (यमः) आसीत् — युधिष्ठिरस्य पिता — यः पुत्रं परीक्षितुम् आगतः आसीत्।
   शब्दार्थ: अतीव = very much; प्रसन्नः सन् = being pleased; अजीवयत् = revived; वस्तुतः = in truth; आसीत् = was; परीक्षितुम् = to test; आगतः = come.
   Translation: Greatly pleased, the Yaksha revived all four brothers. That Yaksha was in truth Dharma (Yama), Yudhishthira's own father, who had come to test his son.
   सारः (Moral): Dharma protects the one who upholds dharma — 'धर्मो रक्षति रक्षितः'. Wisdom, patience and righteousness win where mere strength fails.

Famous प्रश्न-उत्तर verses (शब्दार्थ सहित)

Verse 1 — किमाश्चर्यम् (What is the most wonderful thing?)
   अहन्यहनि भूतानि गच्छन्ति यममन्दिरम् ।
   शेषाः स्थावरमिच्छन्ति किमाश्चर्यमतः परम् ॥
   शब्दार्थ: अहन्यहनि = day after day; भूतानि = living beings; गच्छन्ति = go; यममन्दिरम् = to the abode of Yama (death); शेषाः = the rest (who remain); स्थावरम् = permanence, (to live) forever; इच्छन्ति = wish; किम् आश्चर्यम् अतः परम् = what is more wonderful than this?
   Translation: Day after day living beings go to the abode of Death; yet those who remain wish to live for ever — what is more wonderful than this?
   सारः (Moral): We see death every day, yet act as if we were immortal. Remember your mortality and live wisely and righteously.

Verse 2 — कः पन्थाः (What is the (true) path?)
   तर्कोऽप्रतिष्ठः श्रुतयो विभिन्ना नैको ऋषिर्यस्य मतं प्रमाणम् ।
   धर्मस्य तत्त्वं निहितं गुहायां महाजनो येन गतः स पन्थाः ॥
   शब्दार्थ: तर्कः = reasoning/logic; अप्रतिष्ठः = without firm foundation; श्रुतयः = the scriptures; विभिन्नाः = differing; न एकः ऋषिः = not (only) one sage; यस्य मतं प्रमाणम् = whose opinion is authoritative; धर्मस्य तत्त्वम् = the essence of dharma; निहितं गुहायाम् = hidden in a cave (i.e. deep, subtle); महाजनः = the great/noble people; येन गतः = by which (they) have gone; सः पन्थाः = that is the path.
   Translation: Logic has no firm ground, the scriptures differ, there is no single sage whose word is final; the truth of dharma is hidden in a cave — the (right) path is that which the great and noble have followed.
   सारः (Moral): When rules seem to conflict, follow the tested path of the wise and good (महाजन).

Verse 3 — माता गुरुतरा (Question and answer)
   Question (यक्षः): किं स्विद् गुरुतरं भूमेः? किं स्विद् उच्चतरं नभः?
                     किं स्विद् शीघ्रतरं वायोः? किं स्विद् बहुतरं तृणात्?
   Answer (युधिष्ठिरः): माता गुरुतरा भूमेः खात् पितोच्चतरस्तथा ।
                       मनः शीघ्रतरं वायोश्चिन्ता बहुतरी तृणात् ॥
   शब्दार्थ: गुरुतरम् = heavier/greater; भूमेः = than the earth; उच्चतरम् = higher; नभः/खात् = than the sky; शीघ्रतरम् = faster; वायोः = than the wind; बहुतरम् = more numerous; तृणात् = than grass; माता = mother; पिता = father; मनः = the mind; चिन्ता = worry/anxiety.
   Translation: (Q) What is heavier than the earth? What is higher than the sky? What is faster than the wind? What is more numerous than blades of grass? (A) The mother is heavier than the earth; the father is higher than the sky; the mind is faster than the wind; and worries are more numerous than grass.
   सारः (Moral): Honour mother and father above all; and know how restless the mind and how endless worldly worry can be.

Verse 4 — एकपदम् (The single path to each good)
   Question (यक्षः): किं स्विद् एकपदं धर्म्यं? किं स्विद् एकपदं यशः?
                     किं स्विद् एकपदं स्वर्ग्यं? किं स्विद् एकपदं सुखम्?
   Answer (युधिष्ठिरः): दाक्ष्यमेकपदं धर्म्यं दानमेकपदं यशः ।
                       सत्यमेकपदं स्वर्ग्यं शीलमेकपदं सुखम् ॥
   शब्दार्थ: एकपदम् = the one (sure) step/path; धर्म्यम् = leading to dharma; यशः = fame; स्वर्ग्यम् = leading to heaven; सुखम् = happiness; दाक्ष्यम् = skill/dexterity; दानम् = charity/giving; सत्यम् = truth; शीलम् = good character/conduct.
   Translation: (Q) What is the one path to dharma? to fame? to heaven? to happiness? (A) Skill is the one path to dharma; charity is the one path to fame; truth is the one path to heaven; and good character is the one path to happiness.
   सारः (Moral): Cultivate skill, generosity, truth and good conduct — these single virtues lead to duty, fame, heaven and happiness.

Verse 5 — किं हित्वा (By giving up what...?)
   Question (यक्षः): किं नु हित्वा प्रियो भवति? किं नु हित्वा न शोचति?
                     किं नु हित्वार्थवान् भवति? किं नु हित्वा सुखी भवेत्?
   Answer (युधिष्ठिरः): मानं हित्वा प्रियो भवति क्रोधं हित्वा न शोचति ।
                       कामं हित्वार्थवान् भवति लोभं हित्वा सुखी भवेत् ॥
   शब्दार्थ: हित्वा = having given up; प्रियः = dear (to others); न शोचति = does not grieve; अर्थवान् = wealthy/prosperous; सुखी भवेत् = would become happy; मानम् = pride; क्रोधम् = anger; कामम् = desire; लोभम् = greed.
   Translation: (Q) By giving up what does one become dear? by giving up what does one not grieve? by giving up what does one become wealthy? by giving up what would one be happy? (A) Giving up pride one becomes dear; giving up anger one does not grieve; giving up desire one becomes wealthy; giving up greed one becomes happy.
   सारः (Moral): The four inner enemies — pride, anger, desire and greed — must be conquered by self-control (संयमः) to gain love, peace, contentment and happiness.

व्याकरणम् — A little grammar from the lesson (English explanation, Devanagari examples)

(A) सन्धि (Sandhi — the joining of sounds). Where two sounds meet they often combine. Examples from the verses:
  • किम् + आश्चर्यम् → किमाश्चर्यम् (म् + आ join). Split back (सन्धि-विच्छेद) as किम् + आश्चर्यम्.
  • न + एकः → नैकः (अ + ए = ऐ, वृद्धि-सन्धि) — 'not one'.
  • पिता + उच्चतरः → पितोच्चतरः (आ + उ = ओ, गुण-सन्धि) — 'the father (is) higher'.
  • हित्वा + अर्थवान् → हित्वार्थवान् (आ + अ = आ, दीर्घ-सन्धि).
  • तर्कः + अप्रतिष्ठः → तर्कोऽप्रतिष्ठः (visarga: अः + अ = ओ, with अवग्रह ऽ).
  • दानम् + एकपदम् → दानमेकपदम् (म् joins with the following vowel).
Being able to SPLIT a joined form (सन्धि-विच्छेद) is a key reading skill.

(B) विभक्ति (Vibhakti — case endings). Using the a-stem यक्ष / राम as a model, and words from the verses:
  • प्रथमा (nominative, subject): यक्षः 'the Yaksha', माता 'the mother', मनः 'the mind'.
  • द्वितीया (accusative, object): प्रश्नान् 'the questions', जलम् 'water', भ्रातॄन् 'the brothers'.
  • तृतीया (instrumental, 'by/with'): मृगेण 'by a deer', प्रज्ञया 'with wisdom'.
  • पञ्चमी (ablative, 'than/from'): भूमेः 'than the earth', वायोः 'than the wind', तृणात् 'than grass'. In comparisons Sanskrit uses पञ्चमी for 'than'.
  • षष्ठी (genitive, 'of'): धर्मस्य 'of dharma', यक्षस्य 'of the Yaksha', कुन्त्याः 'of Kunti'.
  • सप्तमी (locative, 'in/at'): वने 'in the forest', गुहायाम् 'in a cave'.

(C) शब्दरूप (declension — worked example). The masculine a-stem यक्ष declines in प्रथमा as: एकवचन यक्षः (one), द्विवचन यक्षौ (two), बहुवचन यक्षाः (many). Compare राम: रामः / रामौ / रामाः. The feminine ā-stem माता (from मातृ) is the प्रथमा एकवचन subject in माता गुरुतरा भूमेः.

(D) धातुरूप (verb forms). Several verbs appear in लट्-लकार (present) and लङ्-लकार (past). Present लट् of भू (to be/become): प्रथमपुरुष भवति (he/she becomes), मध्यमपुरुष भवसि (you become), उत्तमपुरुष भवामि (I become). Present of गम् (to go): गच्छति / गच्छसि / गच्छामि; in the verse भूतानि गच्छन्ति = 'beings go' (प्रथमपुरुष बहुवचन). Past लङ् forms in the story include अवदत् 'said', अभवत् 'became', अपश्यत् 'saw', अपिबत् 'drank', अददात् 'gave'. The optative विधिलिङ् भवेत् 'would become' appears in लोभं हित्वा सुखी भवेत्.

SUMMARY (सारांश)

In this chapter you read the famous यक्षप्रश्न from the महाभारत (वनपर्व). A brahmin's fire-sticks, carried off by a deer, led the thirsty Pandavas to a lake guarded by a Yaksha. Four brothers, ignoring the Yaksha's warning, drank and fell dead; only युधिष्ठिर calmly answered the Yaksha's dharma-riddles and thereby saved them. His fair choice to revive नकुल — so that both mothers would keep a son — revealed his आनृशंस्य (compassion) and justice, and the Yaksha, who was really धर्म (Yama) in disguise, restored all four. You learned the story in simple Sanskrit with शब्दार्थ, translation and moral; studied five celebrated प्रश्न-उत्तर verses (किमाश्चर्यम्, कः पन्थाः, माता गुरुतरा, एकपदम्, किं हित्वा); and drew grammar from the text — सन्धि and its splitting, the six विभक्ति (with पञ्चमी for 'than' in comparisons), the शब्दरूप of यक्ष, and धातुरूप of भू and गम्. The lasting lesson: wisdom, self-control and dharma are greater than mere strength.

sections.heading: The story of the Yaksha Prashna
bullets: During the Pandavas' forest exile a brahmin's fire-sticks (अरणि) were carried off by a deer, and the brothers, chasing it, grew thirsty.
Nakula, Sahadeva, Arjuna and Bhima each found a lake, ignored the guarding Yaksha's warning to answer first, drank, and fell dead.
Yudhishthira came last, and instead of drinking he calmly agreed to answer the Yaksha's questions.

sections.heading: The Yaksha's dharma-riddles
bullets: किमाश्चर्यम् — what is the most wonderful thing? and कः पन्थाः — what is the true path?
Comparisons: what is heavier than the earth, higher than the sky, faster than the wind, more numerous than grass?
Virtue-riddles: the single path (एकपदम्) to dharma, fame, heaven and happiness; and 'by giving up what' one becomes dear, calm, wealthy and happy.

sections.heading: Yudhishthira's wise answers
bullets: The mother is heavier than the earth and the father higher than the sky; the mind is faster than the wind; worries outnumber blades of grass.
Skill leads to dharma, charity to fame, truth to heaven, good conduct to happiness.
Give up pride to be loved, anger to be free of grief, desire to be content, and greed to be happy.

sections.heading: Themes: dharma, wisdom and self-control
bullets: The किमाश्चर्यम् verse warns that we witness death daily yet live as if immortal — so we must be mindful and righteous.
Pride, anger, desire and greed are inner enemies to be conquered by self-control (संयमः).
Yudhishthira's fair choice of Nakula shows आनृशंस्य (compassion) and justice; the Yaksha was really Dharma, teaching 'धर्मो रक्षति रक्षितः'.

sections.heading: Grammar from the lesson
bullets: सन्धि: न + एकः = नैकः (अ+ए=ऐ), किम् + आश्चर्यम् = किमाश्चर्यम्, पिता + उच्चतरः = पितोच्चतरः; splitting is सन्धि-विच्छेद.
विभक्ति: in comparisons Sanskrit uses पञ्चमी for 'than' — भूमेः, वायोः, तृणात्; other cases as usual (प्रश्नान् द्वितीया, प्रज्ञया तृतीया, धर्मस्य षष्ठी, वने सप्तमी).
शब्दरूप of a-stem यक्ष (प्रथमा): यक्षः / यक्षौ / यक्षाः; धातुरूप of भू (भवति) and गम् (गच्छति).

key_takeaways: The यक्षप्रश्न (Mahabharata, Vana Parva) shows that wisdom and self-control are greater than physical strength.
Four strong brothers fell by ignoring wise counsel; Yudhishthira alone, by calm and righteous answers, saved them.
किमाश्चर्यम्: beings die every day, yet the living wish to live for ever — remember mortality and act wisely.
Honour mother and father: माता गुरुतरा भूमेः, father higher than the sky; the restless mind is faster than the wind.
Give up pride, anger, desire and greed (मान, क्रोध, काम, लोभ) — the four inner enemies — to gain love, peace and happiness.
Truth leads to heaven, charity to fame, skill to dharma, good conduct to happiness (the एकपद virtues).
Yudhishthira's fair choice of Nakula reveals आनृशंस्य; the Yaksha was Dharma himself — 'धर्मो रक्षति रक्षितः'.

glossary.definition: 'The Yaksha's questions'; the Mahabharata episode in which a Yaksha tests Yudhishthira with riddles on dharma and wisdom.
A nature-spirit or demigod; here the guardian of the lake, who is really Dharma (Yama) in disguise.
The 'Forest Book' of the Mahabharata, in which the यक्षप्रश्न episode occurs during the Pandavas' exile.
The wooden fire-churning sticks used to kindle the sacred fire; their loss begins the story.
A lake or pool; the water-body guarded by the Yaksha.
'What is the most wonderful thing?'; answered by the verse that we see death daily yet wish to live for ever.
'The one (sure) step or path'; the single virtue that leads to dharma, fame, heaven or happiness.
Righteousness, duty or moral law; also the deity Dharma (Yama) who tests Yudhishthira.
Self-control or restraint; the mastering of pride, anger, desire and greed praised in the verses.
Non-cruelty or compassion; the fairness Yudhishthira shows in choosing to revive Nakula.
Wisdom or discerning intelligence; by which Yudhishthira answers all the Yaksha's questions.
The joining/merging of sounds where two words meet, e.g. न + एकः = नैकः.
A noun's case ending; in comparisons Sanskrit uses पञ्चमी (ablative) for 'than', e.g. भूमेः 'than the earth'.
The conjugation of a verb-root, e.g. भू → भवति and गम् → गच्छति in the present (लट्) tense.

worksheet.title: Worksheet — यक्ष-युधिष्ठिर संवादः (NIOS Sanskrit 209, Chapter 12)
worksheet.instructions: Attempt all questions. Write Sanskrit words in Devanagari and give your explanations in English. Refer to the story and verses in the lesson where needed.

questions.question: In three or four sentences, narrate how the यक्षप्रश्न episode began (the brahmin, the deer and the thirsty Pandavas).
questions.answer: During their forest exile, a brahmin came to the Pandavas and said a deer had carried off his fire-churning sticks (अरणि). The Pandavas chased the deer to recover them, but it disappeared, and the brothers became tired and thirsty. Searching for water, they came upon a lake guarded by a Yaksha — and so the episode of questions began.
questions.explanation: Sets the frame: brahmin's अरणि, the chase, thirst, the guarded lake.

questions.question: Why did the four younger Pandava brothers die at the lake, and what does this teach?
questions.answer: Each of the four — Nakula, Sahadeva, Arjuna and Bhima — reached the lake, ignored the Yaksha's warning to answer his questions before drinking, drank the water, and fell dead. It teaches that even the strong and skilful come to ruin when they act heedlessly (प्रमादः) and ignore wise counsel.
questions.explanation: Heedlessness leads to ruin even for the strong.

questions.question: Give the शब्दार्थ (English word meaning) of each: यक्षः, सरः, जलम्, माता, मनः.
questions.answer: यक्षः = a Yaksha (nature-spirit / demigod); सरः = a lake; जलम् = water; माता = mother; मनः = the mind.
questions.explanation: Core vocabulary from the story and verses.

questions.question: Explain the meaning of the verse 'माता गुरुतरा भूमेः... मनः शीघ्रतरं वायोः...'.
questions.answer: It means: the mother is heavier (greater) than the earth; the father is higher than the sky; the mind is faster than the wind; and worries are more numerous than blades of grass. The verse teaches us to honour our parents above all and reminds us how restless the mind and how endless worldly worry can be.
questions.explanation: Whole-verse meaning plus its lesson about parents and the mind.

questions.question: Narrate the full story of the Yaksha-Yudhishthira dialogue, ending with the Yaksha's true identity.
questions.answer: During the Pandavas' forest exile, a brahmin's fire-sticks (अरणि) were carried off by a deer. The five brothers chased it but lost it, and grew thirsty. Yudhishthira sent Nakula for water; Nakula found a lake, but an unseen Yaksha warned him to answer questions before drinking. Nakula ignored the warning, drank, and died. One by one Sahadeva, Arjuna and Bhima did the same and also fell dead. Finally Yudhishthira arrived, grieved to see his brothers dead, and calmly agreed to answer the Yaksha. He wisely answered many questions on dharma — that the mother is heavier than the earth, the mind faster than the wind, truth the path to heaven, and that giving up greed brings happiness. Pleased, the Yaksha offered to revive one brother. Yudhishthira chose Nakula, so that Madri (his stepmother) would also keep a living son, showing fairness. Delighted by this compassion, the Yaksha revived all four brothers. The Yaksha was really Dharma (Yama), Yudhishthira's own father, who had come to test him — proving that 'dharma protects the one who protects dharma'.
questions.explanation: Complete narration with the आनृशंस्य choice and the reveal of Dharma.

questions.question: Take the verse 'किं नु हित्वा प्रियो भवति...' (question) and 'मानं हित्वा प्रियो भवति...' (answer). Give the word meanings and explain the message.
questions.answer: शब्दार्थ: हित्वा = having given up; प्रियः = dear; न शोचति = does not grieve; अर्थवान् = wealthy; सुखी भवेत् = would become happy; मानम् = pride; क्रोधम् = anger; कामम् = desire; लोभम् = greed. Meaning: the Yaksha asks — by giving up what does one become dear, free of grief, wealthy and happy? Yudhishthira answers: by giving up pride one becomes dear to others; by giving up anger one no longer grieves; by giving up desire one becomes prosperous (content); by giving up greed one becomes happy. The message is that the four inner enemies — pride, anger, desire and greed — must be conquered through self-control, for their conquest brings love, peace, contentment and happiness.
questions.explanation: Word meanings plus the 'four inner enemies' teaching.

questions.question: What is the most wonderful thing (किमाश्चर्यम्) according to Yudhishthira? Explain in one or two sentences.
questions.answer: Yudhishthira says the most wonderful thing is that, although living beings go to the abode of Death day after day, those who remain still wish to live for ever — people see death everywhere yet act as if they were immortal.
questions.explanation: The किमाश्चर्यम् verse on human forgetfulness of mortality.

questions.question: Do the सन्धि-विच्छेद (split) of: (a) किमाश्चर्यम् (b) नैकः.
questions.answer: (a) किमाश्चर्यम् = किम् + आश्चर्यम् (म् joins with आ). (b) नैकः = न + एकः (अ + ए = ऐ, वृद्धि-सन्धि).
questions.explanation: Splitting joined forms back into their words.

questions.question: State the विभक्ति (case) and its sense for each word: भूमेः, वायोः, वने.
questions.answer: भूमेः = पञ्चमी (ablative), used for 'than the earth' in comparison. वायोः = पञ्चमी (ablative), 'than the wind'. वने = सप्तमी (locative), 'in the forest'.
questions.explanation: पञ्चमी marks 'than' in comparison; सप्तमी marks place.

questions.question: Why did Yudhishthira choose to revive Nakula, and what virtue does this reveal? Discuss.
questions.answer: When the Yaksha offered to revive only one brother, Yudhishthira chose Nakula rather than the mighty Bhima or the heroic Arjuna. He reasoned that he himself, a son of Kunti, was alive, so it was only fair that at least one son of Madri (his stepmother) should also live. By putting justice and equal love for both mothers above his own advantage in battle, Yudhishthira revealed आनृशंस्य — non-cruelty, compassion and impartiality. This selfless fairness so pleased the Yaksha (who was really Dharma) that he revived all four brothers. The choice shows that true dharma means fairness and compassion even at personal cost.
questions.explanation: Explains the fairness to both mothers and the virtue of आनृशंस्य.

questions.question: During which period of the Pandavas' lives does the यक्षप्रश्न take place?
questions.explanation: The episode occurs during the twelve-year forest exile in the Vana Parva.

questions.explanation: The यक्षप्रश्न is told in the Vana (Forest) Parva.

questions.question: What did a deer carry off, starting the episode?
questions.explanation: The deer carried away the brahmin's अरणि, prompting the chase.

questions.question: Who first came to the Pandavas with a complaint?
questions.explanation: A brahmin sought the return of his lost fire-sticks.

questions.question: Which brother was sent first to fetch water?
questions.explanation: Yudhishthira first sent Nakula to find water.

questions.question: What did the brothers find in the forest?
questions.explanation: They found a beautiful lake guarded by a Yaksha.

questions.question: Who guarded the lake?
questions.explanation: An unseen Yaksha guarded the water and set the condition of answering questions.

questions.question: What happened to the four brothers who drank without answering?
questions.explanation: Ignoring the warning, each drank and died instantly.

questions.question: Who alone answered the Yaksha's questions?
questions.explanation: Only Yudhishthira paused to answer the riddles.

questions.question: When allowed to revive one brother, whom did Yudhishthira choose?
questions.explanation: He chose Nakula, a son of Madri.

questions.question: Why did Yudhishthira choose Nakula rather than Bhima or Arjuna?
options: so that both mothers (Kunti and Madri) would each keep a living son
questions.answer: so that both mothers (Kunti and Madri) would each keep a living son

questions.explanation: The Yaksha was Dharma himself, come to test his son.

questions.question: 'किमाश्चर्यम्' asks

questions.answer: what is the most wonderful thing?
questions.explanation: किम् आश्चर्यम् = 'what is the wonder/most wonderful thing'.

questions.question: In the किमाश्चर्यम् verse, where do beings go 'day after day'?
questions.explanation: अहन्यहनि भूतानि गच्छन्ति यममन्दिरम् — beings go daily to death's abode.

questions.question: 'कः पन्थाः' means
questions.explanation: पन्थाः = path/way.

questions.question: According to the answer, the true path (पन्थाः) is
options: the one shown by logic alone
the one that the great and noble (महाजन) have followed
the one written in a single book
questions.answer: the one that the great and noble (महाजन) have followed
questions.explanation: महाजनो येन गतः स पन्थाः — follow the path of the wise and good.

questions.question: 'किं स्विद् गुरुतरं भूमेः' asks what is heavier than
questions.explanation: भूमेः = than the earth (पञ्चमी of comparison).

questions.question: The Yaksha asks what is faster than
questions.explanation: किं स्विद् शीघ्रतरं वायोः — faster than the wind.

questions.question: 'किं स्विद् बहुतरं तृणात्' asks what is more numerous than
questions.explanation: तृणात् = than grass (the answer is 'worries').

questions.question: Which virtue does the riddle call 'एकपदं स्वर्ग्यम्' (the one path to heaven)?
questions.explanation: सत्यमेकपदं स्वर्ग्यम् — truth is the one path to heaven.

questions.question: 'किं नु हित्वा सुखी भवेत्' asks: by giving up what does one become happy?

questions.question: The Yaksha's questions to Yudhishthira were mainly about

questions.question: 'माता गुरुतरा भूमेः' means the mother is heavier/greater than
questions.explanation: माता गुरुतरा भूमेः — mother is greater than the earth.

questions.question: 'मनः शीघ्रतरं वायोः' — the mind is faster than

questions.question: 'चिन्ता बहुतरी तृणात्' means ____ are more numerous than grass.

questions.question: The deaths of Bhima and Arjuna at the lake teach that

questions.question: How did the यक्षप्रश्न episode begin?
questions.answer: During the Pandavas' forest exile, a brahmin's fire-churning sticks (अरणि) were carried off by a deer. The brothers chased the deer to recover them, lost it, and grew thirsty — leading them to the Yaksha's lake.
questions.explanation: The brahmin's अरणि and the chase begin the story.

questions.question: What happened at the lake to the four younger brothers, one after another?
questions.answer: Each brother — first Nakula, then Sahadeva, Arjuna and Bhima — reached the lake and was warned by the unseen Yaksha to answer his questions before drinking. Each ignored the warning, drank the water, and fell dead on the spot. Thus all four lay dead when Yudhishthira arrived.
questions.explanation: All four ignored the warning and died in turn.

questions.question: Who was the Yaksha really, and why had he come?
questions.answer: The Yaksha was really Dharma (Yama), Yudhishthira's own father. He had taken the form of a Yaksha to test his son's wisdom and righteousness. Pleased with Yudhishthira's answers and his fairness, he revived all four brothers.
questions.explanation: The Yaksha = Dharma, come to test Yudhishthira.

questions.question: Write, in Devanagari, the Yaksha's question 'किमाश्चर्यम्' verse (first line).
questions.explanation: The opening line of the किमाश्चर्यम् verse.

questions.question: What does the riddle 'किं स्विद् गुरुतरं भूमेः...' ask? Name any two of its comparisons.
questions.answer: It asks a set of comparisons: what is heavier (greater) than the earth, higher than the sky, faster than the wind, and more numerous than blades of grass. (Any two, e.g. 'heavier than the earth' and 'faster than the wind'.)
questions.explanation: The four-fold comparison riddle.

questions.question: What does the riddle 'किं नु हित्वा...' ask about?
questions.answer: It asks: by giving up what does a person become dear to others, free of grief, wealthy, and happy? The answer names the four things to give up — pride, anger, desire and greed.
questions.explanation: The 'by giving up what' riddle about the four inner enemies.

questions.question: Explain Yudhishthira's answer 'माता गुरुतरा भूमेः खात् पितोच्चतरस्तथा...'.
questions.answer: Yudhishthira answers that the mother is heavier (greater) than the earth, the father is higher than the sky, the mind is faster than the wind, and worries are more numerous than blades of grass. The verse honours parents above all and shows how restless the mind and how endless worldly worry are.
questions.explanation: Meaning of the four answers with their lesson.

questions.question: According to the 'मानं हित्वा...' verse, what should one give up to become (a) dear and (b) happy?
questions.answer: (a) One should give up pride (मान) to become dear to others. (b) One should give up greed (लोभ) to become happy.
questions.explanation: Pride → dear; greed → happy.

questions.question: State the एकपद (single-path) answers for dharma and for heaven.
questions.answer: Skill/dexterity (दाक्ष्यम्) is the one path to dharma; and truth (सत्यम्) is the one path to heaven (स्वर्ग्यम्).
questions.explanation: दाक्ष्यम् → dharma; सत्यम् → heaven.

questions.question: Give the शब्दार्थ of: यक्षः, सरः, जलम्.
questions.answer: यक्षः = a Yaksha (nature-spirit / demigod); सरः = a lake; जलम् = water.
questions.explanation: Vocabulary from the story setting.

questions.question: Give the शब्दार्थ of: क्रोधः, लोभः, मानः.
questions.answer: क्रोधः = anger; लोभः = greed; मानः = pride.
questions.explanation: Three of the four inner enemies.

questions.question: Give the शब्दार्थ of: माता, पिता, मनः.
questions.answer: माता = mother; पिता = father; मनः = the mind.
questions.explanation: Vocabulary from the 'माता गुरुतरा' verse.

questions.question: Explain the moral of the verse 'मानं हित्वा प्रियो भवति...'.
questions.answer: The verse teaches that four inner enemies must be conquered by self-control: giving up pride (मान) makes one dear to others; giving up anger (क्रोध) frees one from grief; giving up desire (काम) brings contentment and prosperity; and giving up greed (लोभ) brings happiness. The moral is that inner discipline, not outward gain, is the road to love, peace and joy.
questions.explanation: The four inner enemies and their conquest.

questions.question: What does the episode teach about self-control (संयमः)?
questions.answer: It teaches that self-control is greater than physical strength. The strong brothers acted rashly and died, while Yudhishthira, by calm restraint and wisdom, answered the Yaksha and saved them. Mastering the restless mind and the inner enemies (pride, anger, desire, greed) is the mark of true greatness.
questions.explanation: Restraint and wisdom triumph over rash strength.

questions.question: How does Yudhishthira's choice to revive Nakula show आनृशंस्य (compassion / fairness)?
questions.answer: Offered the life of only one brother, Yudhishthira did not choose the strongest (Bhima) or the greatest warrior (Arjuna) for his own benefit. Reasoning that he, a son of Kunti, was already alive, he asked that Nakula — a son of Madri — be revived, so that both mothers would keep a living son. This impartial, compassionate fairness is आनृशंस्य: placing justice and equal love above personal advantage.
questions.explanation: Fairness to both mothers over self-interest.

questions.question: Do the सन्धि-विच्छेद of: (a) किमाश्चर्यम् (b) नैकः.
questions.answer: (a) किमाश्चर्यम् = किम् + आश्चर्यम् (म् joins आ). (b) नैकः = न + एकः (अ + ए = ऐ, वृद्धि-सन्धि).
questions.explanation: Splitting joined forms into words.

questions.question: Join by sandhi: (a) पिता + उच्चतरः (b) हित्वा + अर्थवान्.
questions.answer: (a) पिता + उच्चतरः = पितोच्चतरः (आ + उ = ओ, गुण-सन्धि). (b) हित्वा + अर्थवान् = हित्वार्थवान् (आ + अ = आ, दीर्घ-सन्धि).
questions.explanation: गुण and दीर्घ sandhi joins.

questions.question: What is सन्धि, and what is सन्धि-विच्छेद? Give one example each from the lesson.
questions.answer: सन्धि is the joining/merging of sounds where two words meet — e.g. न + एकः = नैकः. सन्धि-विच्छेद is the splitting of such a joined form back into its separate words — e.g. किमाश्चर्यम् = किम् + आश्चर्यम्.
questions.explanation: Definition of joining vs splitting with examples.

questions.question: Give the विभक्ति (case) and its sense for: भूमेः and वायोः.
questions.answer: Both भूमेः and वायोः are पञ्चमी (ablative), used in comparison to mean 'than' — 'than the earth' and 'than the wind'. In Sanskrit the standard of comparison takes the पञ्चमी विभक्ति.
questions.explanation: पञ्चमी marks 'than' in comparison.

questions.question: Write the शब्दरूप of यक्ष in प्रथमा विभक्ति (all three numbers).
questions.answer: प्रथमा: एकवचन यक्षः, द्विवचन यक्षौ, बहुवचन यक्षाः.
questions.explanation: Declension of the a-stem यक्ष, nominative.

questions.question: Write the धातुरूप of √भू (लट्-लकार) in the three singular persons.
questions.answer: प्रथमपुरुष एकवचन भवति (he/she becomes); मध्यमपुरुष एकवचन भवसि (you become); उत्तमपुरुष एकवचन भवामि (I become).
questions.explanation: Present-tense singular of √भू.

questions.question: Translate into English: 'महाजनो येन गतः स पन्थाः'.
questions.answer: 'The path (पन्थाः) is that (सः) by which (येन) the great and noble people (महाजनः) have gone (गतः)' — i.e. the right way is the one the wise and good have followed.
questions.explanation: Follow the tested path of the noble.

questions.question: Narrate the story of the यक्षप्रश्न from beginning to end, ending with the Yaksha's true identity.
questions.answer: During their forest exile, a brahmin came to the Pandavas saying a deer had carried off his fire-churning sticks (अरणि). The brothers chased the deer but lost it and grew thirsty. Yudhishthira sent Nakula for water; Nakula found a lake, but an unseen Yaksha warned him to answer questions before drinking. Ignoring the warning, Nakula drank and fell dead. Sahadeva, Arjuna and Bhima came in turn, each ignored the Yaksha, drank, and died. Finally Yudhishthira arrived, grieved to find his brothers dead, and calmly agreed to answer the Yaksha. He wisely answered many dharma-riddles — that the mother is heavier than the earth, the mind faster than the wind, truth the path to heaven, and that giving up greed brings happiness. Pleased, the Yaksha offered to revive one brother. Yudhishthira chose Nakula, so that Madri too would keep a living son — a fair, compassionate choice. Delighted, the Yaksha revived all four. He was really Dharma (Yama), Yudhishthira's own father, who had come to test him, proving that dharma protects the one who upholds it.
questions.explanation: Full narration ending with the reveal of Dharma.

questions.question: Write any TWO प्रश्न-उत्तर (question-answer) verses from the lesson in Devanagari and state the point of each.
questions.answer:
1. किं स्विद् गुरुतरं भूमेः? ... — माता गुरुतरा भूमेः खात् पितोच्चतरस्तथा। मनः शीघ्रतरं वायोश्चिन्ता बहुतरी तृणात्॥ — Point: the mother is greater than the earth and the father higher than the sky; the mind is swifter than the wind and worries outnumber grass — honour your parents and know the restless mind.
2. किं नु हित्वा प्रियो भवति? ... — मानं हित्वा प्रियो भवति क्रोधं हित्वा न शोचति। कामं हित्वार्थवान् भवति लोभं हित्वा सुखी भवेत्॥ — Point: give up pride to be loved, anger to be free of grief, desire to be content, and greed to be happy.
questions.explanation: Two verses recalled with their central teaching.

questions.question: Take the verse 'किमाश्चर्यम्' (question) and its answer. Give the word meanings and a full explanation.
questions.answer: Verse: अहन्यहनि भूतानि गच्छन्ति यममन्दिरम्। शेषाः स्थावरमिच्छन्ति किमाश्चर्यमतः परम्॥ शब्दार्थ: अहन्यहनि = day after day; भूतानि = living beings; गच्छन्ति = go; यममन्दिरम् = to the abode of Yama (death); शेषाः = the rest (the living); स्थावरम् = permanence (to live for ever); इच्छन्ति = wish; किम् आश्चर्यम् अतः परम् = what is more wonderful than this. Explanation: To the Yaksha's question 'what is the most wonderful thing?', Yudhishthira answers that although we see living beings dying and going to death's abode every single day, those who are still alive act as if they will live for ever — they forget their own mortality. The greatest wonder is this human blindness to certain death. The verse urges us to remember life's shortness and therefore to live mindfully, wisely and righteously.
questions.explanation: Word meanings plus the lesson on forgetfulness of mortality.

questions.question: Discuss the themes of dharma, wisdom and self-control as shown in the Yaksha-Yudhishthira episode.
questions.answer: The episode teaches that wisdom, dharma and self-control are greater than mere physical strength. The four strong brothers acted heedlessly, ignored righteous counsel, and perished; Yudhishthira alone, by calm restraint (संयमः) and wisdom (प्रज्ञा), paused to answer and thereby saved them. The Yaksha's riddles are all about dharma: mortality (किमाश्चर्यम्), the true path (महाजनो येन गतः स पन्थाः), honouring parents (माता गुरुतरा भूमेः), and conquering the four inner enemies — pride, anger, desire and greed (मानं हित्वा...). Yudhishthira's answers show a mind trained in righteousness. His final choice to revive Nakula, for fairness to both mothers, reveals आनृशंस्य (compassion) and justice above self-interest. When the Yaksha is revealed as Dharma himself, the message is complete: 'धर्मो रक्षति रक्षितः' — dharma protects the one who upholds it. True greatness lies in a wise, self-controlled and righteous character.
questions.explanation: Weaves together dharma, wisdom, self-control and आनृशंस्य.

questions.question: Why is Yudhishthira regarded as wise and righteous? Support your answer from the episode.
questions.answer: Yudhishthira is regarded as wise and righteous because of both his conduct and his answers. When he found his brothers dead, he did not panic or drink rashly; he met the Yaksha's challenge with calm patience and humility, saying he would answer to the best of his understanding. His replies show deep insight into dharma — on mortality, honouring parents, controlling the restless mind, and giving up pride, anger, desire and greed. Above all, when allowed to revive only one brother, he chose Nakula so that both his mothers would keep a living son, placing fairness and compassion (आनृशंस्य) above his own advantage in war. This blend of self-control, wisdom and impartial justice is why Dharma himself was pleased and why Yudhishthira is honoured as धर्मराज.
questions.explanation: Evidence from his calm, his answers and his fair choice.

questions.question: Explain सन्धि and सन्धि-विच्छेद with four examples taken from the lesson.
questions.answer:
सन्धि is the joining/merging of sounds where two words meet; सन्धि-विच्छेद is splitting a joined form back into its separate words. Examples from the lesson:
1. न + एकः = नैकः (अ + ए = ऐ, वृद्धि-सन्धि).
2. किम् + आश्चर्यम् = किमाश्चर्यम् (म् joins the following आ).
3. पिता + उच्चतरः = पितोच्चतरः (आ + उ = ओ, गुण-सन्धि).
4. हित्वा + अर्थवान् = हित्वार्थवान् (आ + अ = आ, दीर्घ-सन्धि).
Being able to both join (सन्धि) and split (सन्धि-विच्छेद) is essential for reading the verses correctly.
questions.explanation: Definition plus four worked examples with rules.

questions.question: Explain the विभक्ति of comparison and the धातुरूप of भू and गम्, with examples from the lesson.
questions.answer: विभक्ति of comparison: in Sanskrit the standard of comparison ('than X') takes the पञ्चमी (ablative) case. In the verse 'माता गुरुतरा भूमेः, मनः शीघ्रतरं वायोः, चिन्ता बहुतरी तृणात्', the words भूमेः ('than the earth'), वायोः ('than the wind') and तृणात् ('than grass') are all पञ्चमी. धातुरूप: √भू (to be/become) in the present (लट्) gives भवति / भवसि / भवामि (he-she / you / I become); its optative (विधिलिङ्) भवेत् appears in लोभं हित्वा सुखी भवेत्. √गम् (to go) gives गच्छति / गच्छसि / गच्छामि; in the verse भूतानि गच्छन्ति = 'beings go' (प्रथमपुरुष बहुवचन). Recognising these forms helps us read the verses accurately.
questions.explanation: पञ्चमी of comparison plus present-tense forms of भू and गम्.

questions.question: Translate and explain the verse 'तर्कोऽप्रतिष्ठः श्रुतयो विभिन्ना... महाजनो येन गतः स पन्थाः'.
questions.answer: Translation: 'Logic (तर्क) has no firm foundation; the scriptures (श्रुतयः) differ from one another; there is no single sage whose opinion is the final authority; the essence of dharma (धर्मस्य तत्त्वम्) is hidden in a cave (i.e. deep and subtle). Therefore the path (पन्थाः) is that which the great and noble (महाजनः) have followed.' Explanation: When Yudhishthira is asked 'what is the true path?', he replies that reasoning alone is unsteady, the sacred texts sometimes disagree, and no one authority settles every doubt — the deepest truth of dharma is not easy to grasp. So the safest guide in life is to follow the tested path walked by the wise and virtuous. It teaches humility about our own reasoning and respect for the example of good people.
questions.explanation: Full translation with the lesson on following the wise.

questions.question:
Read the verse and answer:
अहन्यहनि भूतानि गच्छन्ति यममन्दिरम्।
शेषाः स्थावरमिच्छन्ति किमाश्चर्यमतः परम्॥
(a) Where do beings go day after day? (b) Give the शब्दार्थ of 'भूतानि'. (c) What do the living (शेषाः) wish for? (d) What is the moral?
questions.answer: (a) Day after day beings go to the abode of Yama (death), यममन्दिरम्. (b) भूतानि = living beings. (c) The living wish for permanence — to live for ever (स्थावरम्). (d) Moral: though death is seen daily, people forget their own mortality; we should remember life's shortness and live wisely.
questions.explanation: Comprehension of the किमाश्चर्यम् verse.

questions.question:
Read the verse and answer:
माता गुरुतरा भूमेः खात् पितोच्चतरस्तथा।
मनः शीघ्रतरं वायोश्चिन्ता बहुतरी तृणात्॥
(a) Who is heavier than the earth? (b) In which विभक्ति is 'भूमेः'? (c) What is faster than the wind? (d) State the lesson.
questions.answer: (a) The mother (माता) is heavier/greater than the earth. (b) भूमेः is पञ्चमी (ablative), 'than the earth'. (c) The mind (मनः) is faster than the wind. (d) Lesson: honour mother and father above all, and know how restless the mind and how endless worry can be.
questions.explanation: Comprehension with a case-identification sub-question.

questions.question:
Read the verse and answer:
मानं हित्वा प्रियो भवति क्रोधं हित्वा न शोचति।
कामं हित्वार्थवान् भवति लोभं हित्वा सुखी भवेत्॥
(a) By giving up what does one become dear? (b) Give the शब्दार्थ of 'हित्वा'. (c) By giving up greed what does one become? (d) What is the theme of the verse?
questions.answer: (a) By giving up pride (मान) one becomes dear. (b) हित्वा = having given up / abandoning. (c) By giving up greed (लोभ) one becomes happy (सुखी). (d) Theme: conquer the four inner enemies — pride, anger, desire and greed — through self-control to gain love, peace, contentment and happiness.
questions.explanation: Comprehension of the 'four inner enemies' verse.

questions.question:
Read the verse and answer:
दाक्ष्यमेकपदं धर्म्यं दानमेकपदं यशः।
सत्यमेकपदं स्वर्ग्यं शीलमेकपदं सुखम्॥
(a) What is the one path to heaven? (b) What leads to fame (यशः)? (c) Give the शब्दार्थ of 'शीलम्'. (d) What does the verse teach?
questions.answer: (a) Truth (सत्यम्) is the one path to heaven (स्वर्ग्यम्). (b) Charity/giving (दानम्) leads to fame. (c) शीलम् = good character / conduct. (d) It teaches that single virtues — skill, charity, truth and good conduct — lead respectively to dharma, fame, heaven and happiness.
questions.explanation: Comprehension of the एकपदम् verse.

questions.question:
Read the verse and answer:
तर्कोऽप्रतिष्ठः श्रुतयो विभिन्ना नैको ऋषिर्यस्य मतं प्रमाणम्।
धर्मस्य तत्त्वं निहितं गुहायां महाजनो येन गतः स पन्थाः॥
(a) What is said to be 'without firm foundation'? (b) Do the सन्धि-विच्छेद of 'नैकः'. (c) Where is the essence of dharma said to be hidden? (d) According to the verse, what is the true path?
questions.answer: (a) Logic/reasoning (तर्क) is said to be without firm foundation (अप्रतिष्ठः). (b) नैकः = न + एकः. (c) The essence of dharma is hidden in a cave (गुहायाम्) — i.e. it is deep and subtle. (d) The true path is the one followed by the great and noble (महाजनो येन गतः स पन्थाः).
questions.explanation: Comprehension with a sandhi split of नैकः.

questions.question:
Read the passage and answer:
तुष्टः यक्षः अवदत् — 'तव एकं भ्रातरं जीवयामि; वृणु।' युधिष्ठिरः 'नकुलः जीवतु' इति अवदत्। सः अवदत् — 'अहं कुन्त्याः पुत्रः जीवामि; माद्र्याः अपि एकः पुत्रः जीवतु।'
(a) What did the Yaksha offer? (b) Whom did Yudhishthira choose? (c) Give the शब्दार्थ of 'जीवतु'. (d) What virtue does his choice show?
questions.answer: (a) The pleased Yaksha offered to revive one of Yudhishthira's brothers. (b) He chose Nakula. (c) जीवतु = 'let (him) live'. (d) His choice shows आनृशंस्य (compassion) and fairness — being alive himself (Kunti's son), he wished a son of Madri also to live, placing justice above self-interest.
questions.explanation: Comprehension of the revival passage and its virtue.

questions.question:
Read the passage and answer:
नकुलः तत् वचनम् अवमन्य जलम् अपिबत्, तत्क्षणम् एव मृतः अभवत्। एवमेव सहदेवः, अर्जुनः, भीमः च क्रमेण जलं पीत्वा मृताः अभवन्।
(a) What did Nakula ignore? (b) Give the शब्दार्थ of 'मृतः'. (c) What happened to all four brothers? (d) What lesson does this teach?
questions.answer: (a) Nakula ignored the Yaksha's words/warning (वचनम्) to answer first. (b) मृतः = dead. (c) All four brothers drank without answering and fell dead. (d) Lesson: even the strong and skilful come to ruin through heedlessness (प्रमादः) and ignoring wise counsel.
questions.explanation: Comprehension of the brothers' death passage.

questions.question:
Read and answer (grammar focus):
यदा नकुलः जलं पातुम् इच्छति, तदा अदृश्यः यक्षः अवदत् — 'मा पिब! प्रथमं मम प्रश्नान् उत्तरं देहि।'
(a) Do the सन्धि-विच्छेद of 'किमाश्चर्यम्' (from the verses). (b) Join by sandhi: पिता + उच्चतरः. (c) Give the शब्दार्थ of 'मा पिब'. (d) In which विभक्ति is 'प्रश्नान्'?
questions.answer: (a) किमाश्चर्यम् = किम् + आश्चर्यम्. (b) पिता + उच्चतरः = पितोच्चतरः (आ + उ = ओ). (c) मा पिब = 'do not drink' (मा is the prohibitive particle). (d) प्रश्नान् is द्वितीया (accusative) plural — the object 'the questions'.
questions.explanation: Grammar practice: sandhi split, join, meaning and case.

questions.question:
Read the sentence and answer (grammar focus):
यक्षः बहून् धर्मविषयकान् प्रश्नान् अपृच्छत्। युधिष्ठिरः प्रज्ञया सर्वेषां प्रश्नानाम् उचितम् उत्तरम् अददात्।
(a) In which विभक्ति is 'यक्षः'? (b) In which विभक्ति is 'प्रज्ञया', and what does it mean? (c) Give the शब्दरूप of यक्ष in प्रथमा (three numbers). (d) From which धातु is 'अददात्' derived?
questions.answer: (a) यक्षः is प्रथमा (nominative), the subject. (b) प्रज्ञया is तृतीया (instrumental) — 'with/by wisdom'. (c) यक्षः / यक्षौ / यक्षाः. (d) अददात् ('gave') is from the धातु √दा (to give).
questions.explanation: Grammar practice: cases, declension and verb-root.

questions.question:
Read the passage and answer (vocabulary focus):
पाण्डवाः वने न्यवसन्। एकः ब्राह्मणः आगत्य अवदत् — 'मम अरणयः मृगेण अपहृताः।' पाण्डवाः मृगम् अन्वधावन्, श्रान्ताः तृषिताः च अभवन्।
(a) Give the शब्दार्थ of 'वने'. (b) Give the शब्दार्थ of 'मृगेण'. (c) Give the शब्दार्थ of 'तृषिताः'. (d) What did the brahmin complain about?
questions.answer: (a) वने = in the forest. (b) मृगेण = by a deer. (c) तृषिताः = thirsty. (d) The brahmin complained that his fire-churning sticks (अरणि) had been carried off by a deer.
questions.explanation: Vocabulary comprehension of the opening passage.
